title: Outgoing IAF Chief Tomer Bar Calls for Independent October 7 Investigation at Handover Ceremony — Day 941
detail: On May 5, 2026 (Day 941 / Ceasefire Day 208), outgoing Israeli Air Force Commander Major General Tomer Bar delivered a landmark public call for an independent external investigation into the October 7, 2023 failures at his handover ceremony, where he passed command to his successor Major General Omer Tishler. Bar stated that an external inquiry is 'vital for the IDF, for all security bodies, for the families who paid the highest price, for trust between citizens and the military, and for the state.' IDF Chief of Staff Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir, attending the ceremony, stated that 'like the entire IDF, the air force failed in its mission to defend the State of Israel.' Bar's public call represents a significant break from the Netanyahu government's position — which has consistently resisted forming an independent state commission of inquiry with subpoena power over civilian and political leadership. His remarks carry particular institutional weight as a departing senior commander speaking freely at his farewell ceremony; they echo the earlier resignations of IDF Chief Halevi (January 2025) and Shin Bet Director Ronen Bar (March 2025), who both explicitly accepted responsibility for the October 7 failure. The handover took place against the backdrop of the Supreme Court's July 1, 2026 deadline for the government to establish an investigation framework, and followed the May 3 external IDF panel finding that most internal October 7 probes were 'inadequate.' Bereaved families' groups described the outgoing air force chief's statement as institutional validation of their longstanding demand: that only an independent commission with subpoena power over military and political leadership can deliver real accountability for the 1,195 deaths and 251 hostage-takings of October 7.

media.caption: Outgoing IAF Chief Tomer Bar calls for external October 7 inquiry at handover ceremony — May 5, 2026

title: Hamas-Board of Peace Disarmament Talks Enter Full Deadlock; Trump Gaza Peace Plan Stalls — Day 941
detail: By May 5, 2026 (Day 941 / Ceasefire Day 208), the six-week Board of Peace disarmament initiative had entered total deadlock. Hamas political bureau representatives in Cairo refused the disarmament framework submitted by High Representative Nickolay Mladenov, insisting that Hamas weapons could only be addressed as part of a framework explicitly leading to Palestinian state establishment and requiring full Israeli withdrawal before any disarmament. Hamas submitted a counter-proposal insisting on an immediate Israeli Defense Forces withdrawal from the so-called 'Yellow Line' (the buffer zone along the Gaza border) as a precondition for disarmament talks. Mladenov traveled to Israel on May 5 to meet Prime Minister Netanyahu following consultations in Cairo, seeking to bridge the sequencing impasse. The IDF reported 19 documented ceasefire violations during the April 21–May 5 period — adding to the 2,400+ total violations since October 10, 2025. Foreign Policy reported that Trump's Gaza peace plan had 'stalled' over the disarmament standoff, with no technical or political mechanism for resolving the core sequencing dispute in sight. Hamas pointed to 828+ Palestinian deaths since the October 2025 ceasefire as evidence of ongoing Israeli aggression that justified maintaining armed resistance. The FDD's Long War Journal analysis noted negotiations had 'collapsed completely.' The May 5 impasse followed the May 3 emergency Israeli security cabinet session weighing scenarios for resuming full-scale military operations. With all four Board of Peace deadlines (April 11, 14, 19, and the late-April window) passed without Hamas acceptance, and the July 1 Supreme Court deadline for the October 7 investigation framework approaching, the situation on Day 941 was characterized by simultaneous diplomatic collapse and escalating domestic accountability pressure.

media.caption: Hamas and Board of Peace enter full disarmament negotiations impasse — ceasefire increasingly fragile, May 5, 2026
